text: {"domains":{"block_M":[64,128],"block_N":[64,128],"block_K":[32,64],"num_stages":[2,3],"threads":[64,128],"swizzle":[0,4,8]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":1,"launches":0.5,"pipeline":1.25,"footprint":1.5},"rationale":"Best observed is attempt-06 at 203.69us (block_M=64, block_N=128, block_K=32, stage=2, threads=128, swizzle=8), improving on the 232.89us incumbent when the changed thread domain was finally exercised (128 threads gave 3 blocks/SM instead of 2). History shows: stage=1 under-pipelines (attempts 00/03); block_M=32/block_N=256 with swizzle=64 regressed to 440.81us; swizzle=4 and swizzle=8 tie at 232.89us in the 256-thread region and swizzle=16 regressed, so panel locality is largely a proxy artifact, not a measured win. Revision: keep block_M {64,128}, block_N {64,128} near the confirmed region; block_K {32,64} with 32 the proven winner; stages {2,3} to retain depth near the working point without overspending footprint at the 32KB cap; threads narrowed to {64,128} to consolidate the win at 128 while still testing 64 against the confirmed 128 (256 dropped since it consistently gave 2 blocks/SM and never won). Swizzle kept {0,4,8}: swizzle=0 to re-verify whether serpentine panels help at the new 128-thread config, 4/8 retained as near-tied options, wider panels (16/32/64) dropped as cache-exceeding regressions. Weights unchanged (traffic 1, launches 0.5, pipeline 1.25, footprint 1.5): footprint binds at the cap and pipelining helped, block counts already ample at 2048 square. Validation scope: Metal numerical checks execute exact source/TIR; CUDA binaries are not executed; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements, and proxy cost is only a dimensionless ranking. Next hypothesis: threads=128 with block_M=128 or block_K=64 and stage 2-3 near the attempt-06 tile may further lower latency; if swizzle=0 ties swizzle=4/8 the panel-reuse feature is confirmed non-materializing and can be retired. No claim of global optimality."}
